chapter: Leading his own band in New York
title: Club 78 in 1948 and the Shangrila
summary: A Winchell clipping about Club 78 and Rhapsody in Blue, and the Shangrila where Tony Bennett got his break.

blocks.x: DID YOU HAVE TIME WHEN YOU CAME UP TO SEE ME AT COLUMBIA, EARLY 1960's, 1961, 1962.
I have some in there now, Al Vernon.
Here's his write up from Walter Winchell's column. DON'T JUDGE BOOKS BY COVERS. CLUB 78 NOW WHERE WAS THAT.
That was Club 78 down on Broadway.

GEE, THAT'S RIGHT NEAR WHERE WE ARE. WHERE I USED TO LIVE. STANLEY THE SNUB MOSLEY ASKED THE PATRONS TO CALL THEIR FAVORITES, RHAPSODY IN BLUE, SOMEONE SHOUTED MOSLEY REALIZED THE CUSTOMER WAS SNEERING AT THE BAND SO HE TURNED AROUND AND HAD HIS SMALL BUT COMPETENT OUTFIT PLAY RHAPSODY PERFECTLY NOTE FOR NOTE FROM BEGINNING TO END. NOW WHAT YEAR WAS THIS. WHEN WERE YOU AT THIS CLUB 78?
SHANGRILA, NOW BACK UP WHERE'S SHANGRILA?

Shangrila was right over here in Long Island, that's where a big story came from I also recorded a number for Walter Thornton called he was one of the big three in modeling agencies, Hanover, Powers & Walter Thornton and I did this, I had it on the show the other day. Joe Franklin had it on also. Pinup girl and he brought Bob Hope out to the Shangrila to hear me, Bob wanted some----, he thought and it was on a Monday nite and I was off and it was a trio in the front and the guitar player and they sat there at the bar for a minute and the listened to this guy and you know was guitar, a little guy by the name of Anthony Benedetti. That's when Tony Bennett got his break. I was off that nite. Bob took him and recorded him and
Just as you cross the Triborough Bridge in Astoria you make a left.
